property_summary: After a deposit of 1 Wei, the reference contract catches that credit[msg.sender] is 0 (since it's an unsigned integer, oCredit cannot be negative), so it skips the if-block and does not transfer Ether; the buggy contract uses '>=0', which is always true, so it attempts to transfer 0 Wei but underflows balance (since balance is 1 but oCredit is 0), causing a revert on 'balance -= oCredit' because balance becomes 0 - 0? Actually the underflow is in balance? Wait, let's compute: after deposit(1), credit[addr]=1, balance=1. In buggy version: oCredit = credit[msg.sender] = 1. Since 1 >= 0, it enters. Then balance = 1 - 1 = 0, credit set to 0, call sends 1 wei. That works fine. Let me think of a case where the bug matters: If the user never deposited, credit[addr]=0. In reference: oCredit = 0, checks (0 > 0) false, skips, no revert. In buggy: checks (0 >= 0) true, enters, then balance -= 0 (ok), credit[msg.sender]=0 (no change), then calls msg.sender with value 0 — a zero-value call succeeds. So no revert. But we need observable divergence: the buggy version will always execute the call even when credit is 0, while reference does not. That can be observed by checking whether a call to a malicious recipient that reverts on receive causes a revert in buggy but not in reference. So scenario: user with zero credit calls withdrawAll, the reference does not make a call (so no revert), the buggy makes a call (reverts). We catch the revert in a try/catch: reference returns true (no revert), buggy returns false (revert). So assertTrue(ok) passes on reference, fails on buggy. The concrete input: no prior deposit, any user (e.g., address(0x123)) and the recipient contract (the test itself) reverts on receive. We set up the test contract to have a receive function that reverts. But the test contract itself is InvMutTest. We need to make the msg.sender (address that calls withdrawAll) be a contract that reverts on receive. We can create a separate contract inside the test file? No, only one contract allowed: InvMutTest. So we use vm.prank with a address that is a contract we deploy? Not allowed extra contracts. Alternatively, we can set up the caller to be an externally owned account (EOA) — an EOA always accepts Ether without reverting. That doesn't differentiate. But we can make the call to a contract that reverts? We can use address(this) as the recipient? The call is to msg.sender. So if we make the test contract (InvMutTest) the msg.sender, then when withdrawAll calls msg.sender.call{value:...}(), it will trigger this contract's receive/fallback. We can define a fallback in InvMutTest? It's allowed to have a fallback function? The test contract can have receive/fallback, but the problem says 'define no other contract/interface/library' — it doesn't forbid having a receive in InvMutTest. However, the test contract inherits Test; it might interfere? We can do: contract InvMutTest is Test { receive() external payable { revert(); } ... }. That should work. Then we do: vm.prank(address(this)); c.withdrawAll(); and catch the revert: try c.withdrawAll() { ok = true; } catch { ok = false; } and then the assertion assertTrue(ok) checks that the call did not revert. In reference, because credit[this]==0, no call is made, so ok=true. In buggy, because condition 0 >= 0 is true, it executes call, which reverts (since receive reverts), so ok=false. That's a concrete scenario with hard-coded values (no parameters). Deposit not needed; initial state: all zero. The assertion: bool ok = true; try c.withdrawAll() { ok = true; } catch { ok = false; } assertTrue(ok). That fails on buggy. Perfect.
